prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and of its biologically active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B010 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The first round showed that all six of us reached it for reasons that hold up on their own. The incretin arc runs from physiology (Holst), through identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov), to proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor pharmacology (Drucker). It is followed by agonists with replicated benefit in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The mechanism is clear, the evidence is mature and the medical effect is large. The chair's move from Knudsen to Mojsov removes the only split in the opening trios. A citation built on discovery of the hormone's physiology and active form is accurate and does not claim that the laureates made the drugs. A second part would have to be attributable to one to three names without a decisive omission, and nothing else on the shortlist meets that test today.
statement.case_against: The attribution cost is real and I am not hiding it. Knudsen's acylation chemistry produced liraglutide and semaglutide, and a discovery-only trio leaves out the person closest to the drugs patients receive. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide, set against Habener who is not on the credited list, cannot be verified from the record we hold. I am therefore placing a third name on a claim that every member, myself included, has described as unverified. If the committee finds that claim too weak, the honest fallback is either Knudsen in the third place or a two-person prize for Drucker and Holst. A discovery-only trio also leaves the prize open to the criticism that the therapeutic step is credited elsewhere.

responses.point: Sandberg said the Mojsov question should not be called merely unresolved: if the record cannot show she identified the active form independently and early, the fallback is a two-person Drucker and Holst prize, and he would rather accept two than credit a third name on an uncertain basis.
responses.response: He is right that I understated this, and I accept the correction. The supplied record neither establishes nor weakens her priority, so I am relying on the generally described role of the truncated peptide in making a therapeutic rationale possible, not on proof. Where I differ is on the fallback. A two-person prize is not a free default, because it leaves out both the peptide-identification step and the drug-design step. If her claim fell, I would weigh Knudsen for the third place before Drucker and Holst alone. A third name tied to a clearly documented step in the chain is more defensible than a shorter prize that omits one. I keep Mojsov in my configuration only because nothing in the file contradicts her role. I will say plainly that this rests on judgement and not on verification.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to the discovery trio, recorded the omission of Knudsen as a real cost, and said the Prize has honoured drug-enabling work before. He also asked whether the first-round unanimity reflects independent merit judgement or shared anchoring.
responses.response: I agree that the omission is a cost, and I now think I was too quick in round 1 to call acylated analogues a mere development of the discovery. His point on precedent is fair. On anchoring, the six opening rankings put B010 first before any exchange, so the first-place agreement was independent. The third place did show some convergence after discussion, which is the part that deserves scrutiny. I tested it by asking what would change my choice. A documented finding that Mojsov's role was secondary would move me to his earlier trio. Since I have no such evidence, I stay with the discovery trio. I would ask the committee to word the citation so that the discovery is clearly credited and the drugs are not.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius treats CAR-T as mature and clinically confirmed, including in autoimmune disease, keeps B052 as her first alternative, and notes the credit problem from Eshhar and others outside the trio and from Rosenberg's work being adoptive transfer rather than CAR design.
responses.response: I ranked B052 third and put it as an alternative in round 1, and I still regard the clinical evidence as mature. Having read the other statements, I give the attribution objection more weight than I did. Four members question Rosenberg's inclusion, and the person who conceived the chimeric receptor sits outside the credited names. A prize that cannot name the conceptual originator is easy to challenge. I would defend B052 as an alternative if B010 fell, but only after the credited set was reworked, perhaps to June and Sadelain alone with Eshhar considered. Under the record as supplied I would not add it as a second part, because I cannot make a trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg describe the discovery accurately.

responses.point: Perlmann argued that BCL-2 (B005) has the more coherent core of Cory, Adams and Vaux, that the 2002 prize overlap must be answered before it is competitive, and that his own first alternative is B048 because the channelrhodopsin and neuronal-use contributions are distinct.
responses.response: I agree that the Cory and Adams core is coherent, and that the mammalian survival function leading to venetoclax is a different question from the C. elegans genetic pathway. I still keep B005 out of my alternatives because the four credited names, the Vaux and Strasser choice and the Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer claims leave the credit less settled than for B052 or B048. His point about B048 changes my view of it. The channelrhodopsin discovery and the neuronal implementation are separate contributions, and I proposed Nagel, Deisseroth and Boyden without resolving whether Hegemann, Bamberg or Miesenböck should be among the three. That is why I rank B048 as an alternative and not a partner for B010.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is secure enough to name her over Knudsen. This cannot be settled from the supplied record, and Habener's role remains unclear.

Whether a discovery-only trio is acceptable when the clinical benefit rests on acylated analogues made in industry, and whether a citation can credit discovery without implying the laureates developed the drugs.
Whether the committee would accept a two-person prize or Knudsen in the third place if Mojsov's claim were found weaker than assumed.
Whether B052 or B048 could, with a reworked credit, ever stand as a second part. I currently judge that neither can be attributed to three names without a decisive omission.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted candidate. My documented ties are to single-cell and spatial genomics and to co-authors such as Sandberg, Frisen and Betsholtz, none of whom is credited on a shortlisted ballot. My co-authorship record with Sandberg is collegial and does not involve any credited name. I update nothing from round 1 and request no recusal.
